correctness.rationale: Reviewed full face and cellular proof. A family F of graph vertices (edges of K_n) inducing maximum disjointness degree ≤1 either is pairwise intersecting, hence lies in a star or triangle, or contains two disjoint edges and therefore every further edge meets both, so all lie in a four-point, six-edge simplex. The n star simplices form a good cover with nerve complete graph; adjoining triangular simplices for triples gives the two-skeleton of Δ^{n−1}. Every four-set simplex intersects this two-core in an octahedral S² with eight facets. Its relative oriented two-cycle has signed triangle facets (1,-1,1,-1), the usual tetrahedron boundary, and all pairwise four-set overlaps lie in the two-core. Simply connected two-core and π₂≈H₂ prove the attaching maps agree with the three-skeleton of simplex. Thus integral H3=ker ∂3 of rank binom(n−1,4), an equivariant lattice ker(∧⁴Z^n→∧³Z^n)=∧⁴ ker(sum) with natural S_n action; higher/other homology vanishes. Independent exact graph face computations and mod2 chain ranks for n=5,6 yielded Betti_3=1,5 and no other Betti, confirming finite instances. This is an infinite structural proof, not extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The Petersen n=5 special case is already exactly published as S³; explicit priority is credited. Feng–Wang study ordinary (r=1) Kneser independence, Sawant studies r-independence for trees, and the KG(6,2) closed-neighborhood Čech computation concerns an unrelated nerve. No checked prior statement covers all n≥5 plus the natural integral ∧⁴ augmentation module.
residual_risks: An equivalent description as a union of edge stars and tetrahedral octahedral attachments could appear in an unindexed higher-independence survey.
Natural S_n module is integral homology, not necessarily an equivariant homotopy wedge decomposition; finite ranks do not alone establish the all-n theorem.

value.rationale: A uniform integral homotopy and full ground-set permutation representation for a canonical infinite Kneser family, determining an exact natural homology module beyond the previously known n=5 example and giving a useful explicit bridge from higher independence to simplex skeleton.
